plan.title: UC inflamed vs control: DE + GSVA hallmark heatmap
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 12 colon RNA-seq samples (6 UC-inflamed vs 6 control), raw Salmon gene counts, single batch, unpaired, with sample_01 flagged at ~4x below-median library size. The pipeline follows the grounded DESeq2 workflow: sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap) to visualize where sample_01 sits without silently dropping it; minimal pre-filtering; DESeq2 Wald test with explicit control-as-reference and apeglm shrinkage; BH-adjusted results at alpha 0.05. To directly answer the research question — a pathway activity score per sample and a heatmap showing which pathways separate treated from control — we run GSVA on the normalized expression matrix against the MSigDB Hallmark human gene set collection (50 sets, staged locally), producing one activity score per sample per hallmark pathway. We then test each hallmark score between inflamed and control with limma (same design as the DE model) to rank which pathways discriminate the groups, and render a heatmap of the score matrix annotated by condition. A DE step is included because the GSVA/limma pathway test benefits from, and the report should present, the gene-level differential expression context (tested gene universe, fold changes) alongside the pathway-level scores; it also satisfies the grounded procedure for this design. The report consolidates DE diagnostics, GSVA scores, the heatmap, and the limma pathway ranking with full reproducibility metadata.
